newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares rise, gains seen short-lived.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares rise, gains seen short-lived.

text.p: Slovenian shares ended firmer on Thursday, aided by strength in market heavy weights drug maker Lek and port operator Luka, but traders saw the gains as short-lived.
The SBI index rose 0.58 percent or 6.93 points to 1,200.8. This week the blue-chip index has fallen 2.8 percent.
Overall 10 shares rose, four fell and one was flat, while 14 were untraded. Turnover more than doubled to 94.3 million tolars from 37.7 million.
"Prices obviously reached their bottom, I think this correction could extend into the first two days of next week," one broker said.

"I expect shares to fall gradually on poor volumes over the summer, although activity would be boosted by any news about EU treaty ratification," said Goran Brankovic, a trader of Nova Ljubljanska Banka.

Two weeks ago the constitutional court delayed the ratification of the treaty, which was signed in June last year and ordered parliament to change the Slovenian constitution in order to allow foreigners to own real-estate.
Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said on Wednesday he expected parliamentary parties to reach an agreement this week on changing the legislation.
Market participants said that the increase in turnover may look impressive at a glance, but it was still very low compared to levels before February.

In February the central bank blocked foreign investors, ordering them to open custody accounts in order to be able to trade in shares, pushing the index down by over 25 percent and average daily volume to about a tenth of its previous size.
Drug maker Lek rose 1.73 percent to 21,780 tolars on volume of 396 shares.
Luka Koper rose 1.90 percent to 1,610 tolars on volume of 721 shares.
Mineral water producer and health resort holder Radenska was the top gainer, jumping 4.35 percent or 65 tolars to 1,560 on volume of 1,284 shares.

"Radenska is one of the shares on our market that was well underpriced as small shareholders who received their shares in exchange for privatisation vouchers were selling," one trader said. He feared selling could resume before summer as people might cash in their shares ahead of their holidays.

Petrol trader Istrabenz, which is not listed on the SBI index, was by far the most active share, firming 0.81 percent or 22 tolars, to 2,735 tolars on volume of 18,930 shares for total turnover of 52.4 million tolars.
Istrabenz was moved from the OTC segment of Ljubljana bourse to the main market on Monday and has fallen 2.73 percent since then.

"Istrabenz is not worth more than 3,000 tolars at the moment as the state still controls petrol prices. Maybe after some four years if Slovenia joins EU and if petrol prices are liberalized, the share could exceed 4,000," the broker said.
Ordinary shares of trading firm Kovinotehna led the decliners, falling 1.67 percent to 413 tolars on low volume of 196 shares.
